docs.title: 🎯 Project Purpose
docs.text: Cyber Sentinel turns raw DNS traffic into decisions. Every new domain seen on the network is checked against threat intelligence, scored by an AI agent and — if malicious — blocked, without anyone reading logs.

docs.title: 🛡️ Problems Solved
docs.text:
• Analysis fatigue: thousands of DNS queries a day are filtered and scored automatically; only real threats reach a human.
  • Scattered CTI: VirusTotal, ThreatFox and URLhaus results are combined into one 1–5 score with a rationale in English and Polish; Shodan InternetDB and urlscan.io add context (open ports, hostnames, the page, other sites on the same IP).
  • Slow response: confirmed malicious domains are added to the Pi-hole denylist and reported by email straight away.
  • Exposed secrets: all API keys and credentials live in HashiCorp Vault, not in containers or the repo.

docs.title: ⚙️ How It Works
docs.text:
• Rules first, AI second: a rule-based score is computed in PostgreSQL; a Gemini AI agent in n8n reviews it, using past verdicts from pgvector memory, within limits set in the database.
  • Noise filtering: Tranco top domains, a manual allow-list and trusted infrastructure are skipped before any API call; the VirusTotal free quota is paced in the database.
  • Second look: Deep Recon re-assesses high-scored verdicts with domain age (RDAP), certificate history (crt.sh) and a urlscan.io page scan, and e-mails when the score should change.
  • Configuration outside the workflow: thresholds, prompts (versioned), allow-lists and threat levels are edited in the AI Config web UI and stored in the database — the workflow only reads them. Every change is audited.
  • Hardened infrastructure: Raspberry Pi 5, Docker images pinned by digest, Nginx with TLS in front of every service, deployed end-to-end with Ansible.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Cyber Sentinel runs as one Docker Compose stack on a Raspberry Pi 5 (arm64); the same stack runs on amd64 for testing. Everything is deployed with Ansible. PostgreSQL is the only database.

docs.title: 1. DNS Capture
docs.text:
client → pihole → unbound → internet
  • Pi-hole filters ads and known-bad domains, holds the denylist that n8n writes to, and logs every query and answer to pihole.log. It answers LAN clients (dns.listeningMode = ALL, set by playbook 04.6), which reach it through the published port 53 with their own source IP.
  • Unbound resolves recursively, without a third-party resolver.
  • dns_log_processor follows pihole.log and turns it into rows in dns_queries: the query with the real client IP, and its answer — forwarded (reply), from Pi-hole's cache (cached) or blocked (blocked). The Pi-hole API and pihole-FTL.db do not keep the answer IP, which the pipeline needs, so the log is the source.

docs.title: 2. Decision Pipeline (n8n)
docs.text:
One workflow, Automated Domain & IP Reputation Guard, runs every minute and handles one observable (domain + IP) per run, as long as the VirusTotal budget (500 calls/day, 4/min) allows it.

  1. Load configuration — all thresholds, the active prompt and the threat scale are read from the database at the start of each run. Nothing is hard-coded in the workflow.
  2. Pick work — the next observable from v_pending_observables, through claim_next_observable(), which also enforces the VirusTotal budget. Allow-listed domains (Tranco, manual) and pairs analysed in the last cache_ttl_days never get here.
  3. VirusTotal gate — VirusTotal checks the IP. Below vt_gate_min_malicious the observable is closed as clean without spending further API calls or AI tokens.
  4. Enrich — Shodan InternetDB (every IP: open ports, software, CVEs, hostnames). Above the gate also ThreatFox (IP), URLhaus (domain) and earlier urlscan.io scans of the domain's page.
  5. Rule score — compute_threat_score() in PostgreSQL returns a 1–5 score from fixed, auditable rules.
  6. AI agent — a Gemini agent reviews the evidence and the rule score. It has one tool, historical_verdicts: a pgvector search over earlier verdicts. It can move the score by at most ai_max_deviation points and must answer in a fixed JSON schema (score, label, rationale in English and Polish).
  7. Persist — raw CTI payloads (JSONB), the verdict and an audit record of what the agent changed and why. Successful verdicts are embedded and stored back into vector memory.
  8. Act — an email for scores ≥ email_min_score; an automatic Pi-hole denylist entry when VirusTotal detections reach pihole_block_min_vt_malicious and the IP is not trusted infrastructure. Every block attempt is logged.

A second workflow, Deep Recon, runs hourly and re-assesses verdicts scored ≥ recon_min_score with context the main workflow does not collect: domain registration (RDAP), certificate history (crt.sh) and the web page, which urlscan.io loads from its own infrastructure. An AI analyst without tools says whether this confirms the verdict and may propose a score within recon_max_deviation. Verdicts are not changed automatically: the result is stored in deep_recon and e-mailed when the proposed score differs.

Two daily workflows build own Pi-hole blocklists: Blocklist Candidates lets Gemini classify domains whose names look like telemetry or tracking, and Blocklist Publish turns approved entries plus the Pi-hole auto-blocks into list files in the public repository sentinel-blocklists, through one pull request that is merged by hand.

docs.title: 3. AI Configuration
docs.text:
The pipeline's behaviour lives in the cyber_sentinel_ai schema and is changed only through the AI Config web UI (ai-config-ui):

  • settings — thresholds and switches used in the steps above,
  • prompts — versioned, with diff; exactly one version is active,
  • trusted infrastructure, manual allow-list and exclusions,
  • threat level wording,
  • simulator — runs live lookups and shows the score without touching the n8n queue,
  • Deep Recon — results, re-queue and the versioned recon prompt,
  • own blocklists — review queue, list contents, name patterns, the versioned classifier prompt and the publish log,
  • VirusTotal calls used and left today.

The UI connects with its own least-privilege role; every change is written to config_change_log. Details: AI Config UI integration.

docs.title: 4. Platform
docs.text: Area Components Secrets HashiCorp Vault — API keys and credentials are read by n8n at runtime; nothing secret in the repo or the workflow Data PostgreSQL 16 + pgvector; high-volume tables partitioned with automatic retention (Database) Access Nginx with TLS in front of every web UI, UFW, Fail2Ban Monitoring Prometheus, Node Exporter — host metrics for the planned health agent Operations Portainer; images pinned by digest in group_vars/all/images.yml

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
One PostgreSQL 16 instance (postgres_db) with the pgvector and pg_cron extensions. Database cyber_intelligence, two schemas:

Schema Holds Written by cyber_sentinel DNS traffic, CTI results and verdicts — the data dns_log_processor, n8n cyber_sentinel_ai Everything that drives the AI pipeline — settings, prompts, allow-lists, audit, vector memory AI Config UI, n8n, Tranco sync

The SQL lives in config/postgres/ and is applied in this order. Every file is idempotent and re-runs on each deployment.

# File Playbook Creates 1 db_deployment.sql 04.3 cyber_sentinel schema, app role, tables, views 2 db_partitioning_retention.sql 04.3 partitions, retention functions, pg_cron jobs 3 db_ai_pipeline.sql 04.3 cyber_sentinel_ai schema, scoring, allow-list, work queue, API call log and VirusTotal budget, Deep Recon, Failure Guard 4 db_blocklists.sql 04.3 own blocklists: entries, AI classifications, name patterns, classifier prompt, publish log 5 db_ai_config_editor.sql 04.5 AI Config UI role, audit log, guard triggers

Tables

Object What it does dns_queries Every DNS query and answer from Pi-hole's log, with the client IP. query_type: query, reply (forwarded to Unbound), cached (Pi-hole cache), blocked (gravity / denylist). Partitioned by month. threat_indicators Links a DNS query to its verdict; counts re-scans. Partitioned by month. ai_analysis_results Final verdict: score 1–5, label, summary in English and Polish. threat_indicator_details Which CTI provider contributed to a verdict, with a pointer to its raw response. threat_data_raw Raw JSON responses from VirusTotal, ThreatFox, URLhaus, urlscan.io, Shodan InternetDB and RDAP (JSONB). network_events Reserved for IDS / packet-capture events. Partitioned by month. partition_maintenance_log Every partition added or dropped, including failures.

Dictionaries

Object What it does dic_threat_levels The 1–5 scale: wording, recommended action and whether the level counts as malicious. Editable in the AI Config UI. dic_indicator_types Observable types: FQDN, IP, HASH. dic_source_providers CTI providers.

Views

Object Used by v_threat_scale_for_agent The threat scale as text, injected into the AI agent prompt. v_latest_threat_reports Latest verdict per DNS query; base for the Grafana views. v_grafana_* Dashboards: malicious stats, daily trends, hourly DNS traffic, threat alerts, threat explorer. v_pending_analysis Previous work queue, still read by the DNS Traffic dashboard. v_partition_info Rows and size per partition.

ai_analysis_results belongs to cyber_sentinel. The AI schema extends each verdict without changing the CTI tables.

Pipeline configuration — edited in the AI Config UI

Object What it does ai_settings Every threshold and switch the workflows read: VirusTotal budget and gate, scoring limits, AI deviation, cache, email and Pi-hole thresholds, urlscan.io search, Shodan, Deep Recon (recon_*). prompt_templates Versioned system prompt for the AI agent. Exactly one version is active. recon_prompt_templates Versioned system prompt for the Deep Recon analyst. Exactly one version is active. trusted_infrastructure Big providers (by AS owner or domain) whose low-detection noise is ignored and whose score is capped. domain_allowlist Domains never sent for analysis: Tranco top list (weekly) plus manual entries. domain_allowlist_exclusions Platforms where anyone can publish under a subdomain (github.io, ngrok.io, …). They override Tranco entries. v_manual_allowlist The only way to edit the allow-list from the UI — manual rows only. blocklist_name_patterns Name fragments (telemetry, track, …) that make a domain a candidate for AI classification. blocklist_prompt_templates Versioned system prompt for the blocklist classifier. Exactly one version is active. blocklist_entries Own blocklists: one row per domain and list (malicious, tracking, telemetry) with status candidate / approved / rejected, source, expiry and who reviewed it. AI and the malicious sync add rows; the UI approves, rejects and adds manual ones.

Pipeline data — written by n8n

Object What it does v_pending_observables Work queue: new domain + IP pairs, without private IPs, allow-listed domains and pairs analysed in the last cache_ttl_days. api_call_log One row per outgoing CTI / AI request: provider, caller, endpoint, HTTP status, outcome. Partitioned by month, kept 3 months. VirusTotal claims of the main workflow also stop overlapping runs from taking the same pair. vt_lookup_log View on api_call_log (VirusTotal calls of the main workflow); a table until v2.2. api_provider_quota Providers' own usage counters, written hourly by API Usage Monitor (kept 14 days). v_vt_budget VirusTotal calls used today (the higher of the local count and VirusTotal's counter), in the last minute, calls left, reserve, next reset. v_api_usage_today / v_api_usage_daily Usage per provider today with limit and share; calls per day, provider and caller. api_alert_log Providers e-mailed for crossing api_alert_threshold_pct, one row per UTC day. ops_settings Text settings Failure Guard needs while Vault may be down (e-mail sender and recipient). Written by playbook 04.3. workflow_failure_alerts Workflows Failure Guard stopped: failures, first failure, failed node, error. verdict_audit Per verdict: rule score, final score, what the agent changed and why, model, prompt version, evidence. Also the "already analysed" cache. verdict_vectors Vector memory of past verdicts (3072-dim Gemini embeddings) searched by the agent's historical_verdicts tool. pihole_block_log Every automatic Pi-hole block attempt and its result. v_pending_recon Deep Recon queue: verdicts with score ≥ recon_min_score from the last recon_lookback_days, without a recent recon of the same domain. Empty while recon_enabled = 0. deep_recon One row per re-assessed verdict: domain age and registrar (RDAP), certificate history (crt.sh), page scan (urlscan.io links and facts), and the analyst's result — page type, brand, credential harvesting, confirms / contradicts, proposed score and reason (score_changed when it differs from the verdict). v_blocklist_ai_queue Domains waiting for blocklist classification: pattern match, enough queries, not classified, not on a list, not manually allow-listed. blocklist_classifications One AI answer per domain: category, vendor, confidence, breakage risk, reason. A domain here is not sent to the AI again. v_blocklist_published Approved, not expired, not manually allow-listed entries — exactly what goes into the files. blocklist_publish_log One row per publish run: dry run, no change, published (with pull request) or error.

Logs

Object What it does config_change_log Who changed which setting, prompt or list, with old and new values. Append-only. domain_allowlist_sync_log Result of each Tranco sync.

Functions

Object What it does compute_threat_score() Deterministic 1–5 score from VirusTotal, ThreatFox and URLhaus results, with a step-by-step trace. is_allowlisted() Allow-list check; the most specific rule wins. setting() Reads one value from ai_settings; fails on a missing key. sp_sync_domain_allowlist() Applies the weekly Tranco list as a delta; aborts if the list is suspiciously short. claim_next_observable() Returns the next pending observable and logs the claim, or nothing when the queue is empty or the VirusTotal budget is used up. api_call_result() Fills in the HTTP status of the main workflow's VirusTotal claim. api_calls_record() Logs a batch of calls (the Log API calls nodes). api_claim() / api_call_finish() VirusTotal claim and result for the simulator; the only way the UI writes the log. api_quota_record() / api_usage_alerts_due() Stores a provider counter; returns the providers to e-mail today and marks them. recon_requeue() Removes one deep_recon row so its verdict gets a new second look; the only way the UI deletes from that table. blocklist_record_classifications() Stores one AI batch and turns telemetry / tracking answers into review candidates. blocklist_sync_malicious() Copies Pi-hole auto-blocks into the malicious list and extends their expiry. blocklist_render() Full content of the three list files. blocklist_is_protected() TRUE when a manual allow-list entry covers the domain.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Access postgres Superuser; runs the deployment scripts and pg_cron jobs. app role (postgres_user) n8n and dns_log_processor: read/write in both schemas, read-only on the audit log. ai_config_editor AI Config UI only: the configuration objects above, nothing from the data tables. Reads deep_recon, the recon queue, the VirusTotal budget, the API call log and Failure Guard alerts; logs simulator calls through api_claim() / api_call_finish() only. Guard triggers stop it from breaking the pipeline (active prompts are read-only, one prompt of each kind always active, malicious levels stay a contiguous top range).

Passwords come from vault.yml and are copied to HashiCorp Vault.

docs.title: Partitioning and Retention
docs.text:
dns_queries, threat_indicators, network_events and cyber_sentinel_ai.api_call_log are partitioned by month (<table>_pYYYYMM) with a default partition catching anything outside the range. The list lives in cyber_sentinel.partitioned_tables(). Two pg_cron jobs run on the 1st of each month:

Job Time Action evt_drop_old_partitions 02:00 Drops partitions older than 3 months (same for all tables, so links between them stay complete) evt_add_future_partitions 03:00 Creates partitions for the next 3 months 
SELECT * FROM cyber_sentinel.v_partition_info;
SELECT * FROM cyber_sentinel.partition_maintenance_log ORDER BY executed_at DESC LIMIT 20;
SELECT * FROM cron.job_run_details ORDER BY start_time DESC LIMIT 20;

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The whole stack is deployed with Ansible from a control machine. One master playbook, 00_main.yml, runs every step in order; each step can also be re-run on its own.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Control machineTarget server 
sudo apt update && sudo apt install pipx
pipx install --include-deps ansible
pipx inject ansible hvac docker
OS Debian 12/13 or Raspberry Pi OS Architecture amd64 or arm64 (detected automatically) Access SSH key, user with sudo Resources 4 GB RAM, 32 GB disk (the stack uses about 2 GB RAM)

docs.text:

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
All secrets live in ansible/group_vars/all/vault.yml, encrypted with ansible-vault. During deployment they are copied into HashiCorp Vault, where n8n reads them at runtime.

# Service logins
vault_pihole_admin_password: ""
vault_grafana_password: ""
vault_portainer_password: ""
vault_n8n_password: ""

# PostgreSQL
vault_postgres_root_password: ""
vault_postgres_password: ""
vault_ai_config_db_password: ""    # openssl rand -hex 24 (hex only)

# AI Config UI
vault_ai_ui_secret_key: ""         # openssl rand -hex 32
vault_ai_ui_users:                 # password (>= 12 chars) or werkzeug hash
  lukasz: ""

# API keys
vault_virus_total_token: ""
vault_abuse_api_key: ""            # abuse.ch: ThreatFox + URLhaus
vault_gemini_api_key: ""
vault_urlscanio_api_key: ""        # urlscan.io: search (main workflow) + page scans (Deep Recon)
vault_github_blocklists_token: ""  # fine-grained PAT, sentinel-blocklists only: Contents + Pull requests read/write
vault_grafana_api_key: ""

# Email alerts (Gmail)
vault_n8n_user: ""                 # sender address
vault_n8n_gmail: ""                # Gmail app password
vault_n8n_alert_to: ""             # alert recipient (defaults to the sender)

# TLS: one cert/key pair per service behind Nginx
# pihole, n8n, grafana, portainer, firefox, hashicorp_vault, ai_config
vault_pihole_cert: |
  -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----

Encrypt the file and keep the password in ansible/.vault_pass (ignored by git, referenced from ansible.cfg):

ansible-vault encrypt ansible/group_vars/all/vault.yml
echo "your_passphrase" > ansible/.vault_pass && chmod 600 ansible/.vault_pass

Vault keys are shown once

The first run of playbook 06.1 initialises HashiCorp Vault and prints vault_root_token and vault_unseal_keys exactly once. Copy them into vault.yml straight away and keep an offline backup. Losing the unseal keys means losing all Vault data.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
cd ansible
ansible-playbook 00_main.yml --limit rpi5-prod     # production
ansible-playbook 00_main.yml --limit vm-prox-dev   # dev VM

ansible.cfg already sets the inventory and the vault password file, so no extra flags are needed when running from ansible/.

docs.title: Playbooks
docs.text:
Each playbook starts with a header describing its purpose, dependencies and sections — see ansible/ for details.

# Playbook What it does 00.1 00_1_restore_proxmox.yml Restores the dev VM from its latest Proxmox backup. Runs only for vm-prox-dev. 01 01_setup_secrets.yml Renders .env on the host from vault.yml 02 02_setup_security.yml UFW firewall 03 03_setup_system.yml Docker Engine, system packages, Pi 5 fan control 04.1 04_1_prepare_stack.yml Copies the compose file, Dockerfiles, configs and app sources 04.2 04_2_deploy_containers.yml Builds and starts the Docker Compose stack 04.3 04_3_db_postgres.yml PostgreSQL schema, partitioning, AI pipeline schema 04.4 04_4_tranco_allowlist.yml Tranco allow-list: initial load + weekly cron 04.5 04_5_ai_config_editor.yml Database role for AI Config UI, rebuilds ai-config-ui 04.6 04_6_post_config.yml Fail2Ban, Pi-hole, Portainer and n8n accounts, workflow import 05 05_deploy_proxy.yml Nginx reverse proxy with TLS 06.1 06_1_initialize_provision_vault.yml Vault init/unseal, secrets, n8n token, Pi-hole API password 06.2 06_2_n8n_bootstrap.yml n8n community nodes and credentials 06.3 06_3_n8n_api_key.yml Failure Guard: n8n API key (rotated on every run, stored as an n8n credential) and activation. Run after every 04.6. 07 07_setup_monitoring.yml SSD health metrics for Prometheus. Production only, run manually — not part of 00_main.yml.

Re-run a single step the same way:

ansible-playbook 04_3_db_postgres.yml --limit rpi5-prod

Order matters in two places: 04.1 must run before 04.2 (it stages the build contexts), and 04.5 must run after 04.3 (04.3 re-grants table privileges that 04.5 narrows again).

docs.title: Proxmox Restore (optional)
docs.text:
Playbook 00.1 is specific to the author's dev setup and is skipped everywhere else. To use it, add to vault.yml:

proxmox_host: ""         # Proxmox VE host, API on port 8006
proxmox_user_token: ""   # user@realm!tokenid
proxmox_api_secret: ""

The token needs VM power, backup and config rights on the VM and allocate rights on the backup storage; in a home lab PVEAdmin on / is the simple option.

docs.title: After Deployment
docs.text:
Open ports (everything else is denied):

Port Service 22/tcp SSH 53/tcp+udp Pi-hole DNS 80/tcp redirect to HTTPS 443/tcp Nginx

Port 53

Pi-hole answers every client that reaches it (dns.listeningMode = ALL, needed to log LAN devices with their own IP). The host must not be reachable from the internet on port 53 — no port forward on the router — otherwise Pi-hole becomes an open resolver.

Web UIs (<suffix> is prod or local):

Service URL AI Config UI https://ai-config.<suffix> n8n https://n8n.<suffix> Pi-hole https://pihole.<suffix> Grafana https://grafana.<suffix> Portainer https://portainer.<suffix> Vault https://hashicorp_vault.<suffix> Firefox (isolated browser) https://firefox.<suffix>

Add these names to your local DNS (Pi-hole → Local DNS records) pointing at the host.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text: The whole stack is defined in docker/docker-compose-cyber-sentinel.yml. Playbook 04.1 renders it as a Jinja2 template, 04.2 starts it. Secrets come from .env (playbook 01); image versions from ansible/group_vars/all/images.yml, pinned by digest.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
All containers share one bridge network, internal_network (10.10.10.0/24), with static IPs. Except Unbound and Pi-hole, they use Pi-hole as DNS.

docs.title: Exposure
docs.text:
Only DNS is published on the host network. Everything with a web UI is reached through Nginx over HTTPS.

Published Service Why 0.0.0.0:53 tcp/udp pihole DNS for the LAN 127.0.0.1:5678 n8n Loopback only — Docker-published ports bypass UFW 127.0.0.1:8200 vault Loopback only — used by playbook 06.1

All other services have no published ports.

docs.title: Hardening
docs.text:
• ai-config-ui — read-only filesystem, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, 128 MB / 0.25 CPU limit; receives only its own AI_UI_* variables and its own least-privilege database role.
  • vault — IPC_LOCK so secrets are not swapped to disk; TLS terminated by Nginx.
  • firefox — stateless, profile in tmpfs.
  • node_exporter — host /proc, /sys and / mounted read-only.
  • portainer — has the Docker socket, i.e. full control of the host's Docker. Keep it behind Nginx.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Volume Holds postgres_data the cyber_intelligence database n8n_data workflows, credentials, execution history grafana_data users and non-provisioned dashboards prometheus_data metrics history ./config/vault/data Vault storage (bind mount) ./portainer_data Portainer settings (bind mount)

Removing a volume deletes its data. Vault data cannot be recovered without the unseal keys.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: What is planned next. Delivered work is listed in Releases.

docs.title: 1. Sentinel Engram
docs.text:
Sentinel Engram is the long-term memory of Cyber Sentinel: a separate project that loads AI verdicts, DNS activity and Pi-hole blocklists into a Vertex Synapse CTI graph, with a Neo4j view for visual analysis. It reads Cyber Sentinel's database through a read-only role and an SSH tunnel and never writes to it.

Planned on the Cyber Sentinel side:

  • Ship the export in this repo — move db_engram_export.sql (role engram_reader, schema engram_export) and the engram-tunnel user into Cyber Sentinel's playbooks, so a dev deploy no longer removes them.
  • Graph context for the AI agent — n8n queries Synapse (user n8n-agent: read, ai.* tags only) to give the agent history the database does not have: blocklist membership, related domains on the same IP, first-seen dates.
  • Anomaly agent — a scheduled n8n agent compares daily device behaviour in the graph against a baseline and tags findings with ai.*. Device data must be anonymised before it leaves Cyber Sentinel.

docs.title: 2. Agentic Development
docs.text:
Goal: a system that checks itself, corrects its own mistakes and improves its own configuration, with a human approving changes instead of doing them. Each item runs as a separate n8n workflow; workflows hand work to each other through a status-driven queue table. Order below is the planned order.

  1. Health agent — daily check of the pipeline: queue depth, failed AI analyses, pg_cron jobs, aborted Tranco syncs, and host state from Prometheus (see section 6). API usage and 429s come from api_call_log, and stopped workflows from Failure Guard (both in v2.3.0). Sends a short daily report.
  2. Verdict review and auto-unblock — weekly re-scan of verdicts scored 3–5 and of everything blocked in Pi-hole. Blocks get an expiry date; a domain that stays clean is unblocked, one that became malicious is raised.
  3. Analyst feedback — mark a verdict as false positive or true positive in the AI Config UI (or with the cs.fp tag in Engram). Labelled verdicts go into vector memory as confirmed examples.
  4. Prompt and threshold tuning agent — analyses verdict_audit and feedback: where the AI deviates from the rules and why, which rules produce false positives, how often the agent fails. Creates a new prompt version or setting change as an inactive draft, replays it against stored evidence from recent verdicts (no CTI API calls) and shows the difference. Activation stays manual in the AI Config UI.
  5. Retro-hunting — daily download of new ThreatFox IOCs, searched backwards in dns_queries: which device contacted a domain before it was known to be malicious. Needs no VirusTotal calls; can run in parallel with the items above.
  6. Agent-chosen enrichment — CTI sources become tools the agent picks within a budget instead of a fixed sequence. Already in place: urlscan.io search and Shodan InternetDB in the main workflow; RDAP, crt.sh and urlscan.io page scans in Deep Recon. Next: Shodan host details and pivots (needs a paid Shodan membership) as a Deep Recon source.
  7. Engram tools — the Synapse graph as an agent tool and the device anomaly agent (see section 1). Optional at run time: the Engram host is up only a few hours a day, so anomaly analysis runs in batches.
  8. Agent-decided actions — blocking and alerting decided by the agent instead of fixed thresholds, with hard limits enforced by the workflow: never block trusted infrastructure, a daily block limit, every block with an expiry. Depends on item 2, so wrong decisions undo themselves.

Constraints for all items: VirusTotal free tier (500 requests/day), Gemini free tier limits, Raspberry Pi 5 with 8 GB RAM.

docs.title: 3. Device Attribution
docs.text:
• user_devices table mapping internal IPs to devices and owners.
  • Per-device reports and alerts from n8n.
  • Identity signals (Vault audit log, SSH auth log) as a later step.

docs.title: 4. Hardening
docs.text:
• TOTP for web UIs (n8n, Portainer, AI Config UI).
  • Nginx rate limiting and security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options).
  • GeoIP blocking and port knocking for SSH.

docs.title: 5. File Integrity Monitoring
docs.text:
• Hashes of critical files (sshd_config, playbooks, compose) stored in the database.
  • Scheduled comparison; an AI agent decides whether a change looks like administration or compromise and alerts.

docs.title: 6. Monitoring
docs.text:
• Prometheus and node_exporter become the data source for the health agent instead of something to look at: disk usage, Pi temperature, SSD SMART (playbook 07), read by n8n through the Prometheus HTTP API.
  • Grafana will be removed. Its job — showing what happens in the pipeline — is taken over by the n8n agents: the health agent's daily report and alerts, plus operational views in the AI Config UI.

docs.title: 7. Own Blocklists — Follow-ups
docs.text:
The first version shipped in v2.2.0: name patterns, AI classification, review in the AI Config UI and a daily pull request to sentinel-blocklists — see n8n Workflows. Still open:

  • Query-interval pre-filter — regular query intervals per device as a second candidate signal next to name patterns. Real client IPs are in dns_queries since v2.4.0.
  • Category from the main workflow — optional: the main workflow's AI returns the same category (telemetry / tracking) for domains it already analyses and adds hits to the review queue.

docs.title: n8n Workflows
docs.text:
Six workflows in config/n8n/workflows/, all imported by playbook 04.6:

  • Automated Domain & IP Reputation Guard — the main pipeline. Runs every minute and analyses one observable — a domain and the IP it resolved to — per run, as long as the VirusTotal budget allows it (see VirusTotal Budget).
  • Deep Recon — runs hourly (at :20) after the verdict: domain age, certificate history and the web page of high-scored domains, then an AI re-assessment. See Deep Recon.
  • Blocklist Candidates and Blocklist Publish — daily (03:20 and 05:20): own Pi-hole blocklists for malicious, tracking and telemetry domains, published to sentinel-blocklists. See Own Blocklists.
  • API Usage Monitor — hourly (at :05): VirusTotal's own usage counter and the daily usage e-mail. See API Usage.
  • Failure Guard — the Error Workflow of all the others: stops a workflow after failure_guard_threshold failed runs in a row and sends one e-mail. See Failure Guard.

An earlier version is published in the n8n library: Score DNS Threats with VirusTotal, Abuse.ch, HashiCorp Vault, and Gemini.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Load AI configuration] --> B[Pick observable if budget allows<br>claim_next_observable]
    B --> C[VirusTotal: IP]
    C --> S[Shodan InternetDB: IP]
    S --> D{detections ≥<br>vt_gate_min_malicious?}
    D -- no --> E[Rule score] --> F[Clean verdict<br>no AI, no email]
    D -- yes --> G[ThreatFox: IP<br>URLhaus: domain<br>urlscan.io search: domain]
    G --> H[Rule score 1–5]
    H --> I[AI agent<br>Gemini + historical_verdicts]
    I --> J[Parse and clamp score]
    J --> K[Store verdict, audit, raw CTI]
    F --> K
    K --> L[Vector memory]
    K --> M{score ≥ email_min_score?}
    M -- yes --> N[Email alert]
    K --> O{auto-block conditions?}
    O -- yes --> P[Pi-hole denylist + block log]

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Load configuration — one query reads all ai_settings, the threat scale and the active prompt. Every threshold below comes from there and is edited in the AI Config UI.
  2. Pick observable — claim_next_observable() returns the next row of v_pending_observables, or nothing when the VirusTotal budget is used up. Private IPs, allow-listed domains and pairs analysed in the last cache_ttl_days are already filtered out.
  3. VirusTotal — VirusTotal checks the IP; the HTTP status goes into api_call_log right away. A failed lookup (quota, auth, server error) is never scored as clean: the run fails and the observable is retried later. The request is not retried inside the run, so one claim is exactly one VirusTotal call.
  4. Shodan and the gate — every IP is also looked up in Shodan InternetDB (switch shodan_internetdb_enabled): open ports, software, known CVEs, tags and the hostnames Shodan saw on the IP. Free, no API key, no quota; weekly snapshot, non-commercial use only. It is context for the AI agent and the e-mail and does not change the rule score. Below vt_gate_min_malicious detections the observable is then scored by rules only and stored as clean: no further API calls, no AI tokens, no email.
  5. Enrich — ThreatFox (by IP), URLhaus (by domain) and two urlscan.io searches (switch urlscan_search_enabled, scans younger than urlscan_search_days): earlier scans of the domain's page (title, HTTP status, TLS issuer and certificate age, urlscan's verdict) and other sites urlscan saw on the same IP (malicious ones first). All are supporting sources; urlscan.io is only searched, nothing is submitted, and nothing here changes the rule score.
  6. Rule score — compute_threat_score() in PostgreSQL turns the results into a score 1–5 with a step-by-step trace.
  7. AI agent — reviews the evidence and the rule score (details below).
  8. Store — raw responses, verdict, audit record and the embedding for vector memory.
  9. Act — email and Pi-hole auto-block (details below).

docs.title: VirusTotal Budget
docs.text:
The public API allows 4 requests per minute and 500 per day; the daily quota resets at 00:00 UTC. The workflow runs every minute, and claim_next_observable() decides whether this run may call VirusTotal. Used is the higher of two counters: VirusTotal calls in api_call_log today (every caller), and VirusTotal's own counter for the key, read hourly by API Usage Monitor. The second one also sees calls this stack never logged — the dev environment and manual tests use the same key.

Setting Default Meaning vt_daily_limit 500 Calls per day. At the limit the workflow stops until the reset. vt_per_minute_limit 4 Calls in the last 60 seconds. Matters when runs overlap or the schedule runs more often than once a minute. vt_reserve_per_hour 5 Calls kept back per hour left until the reset, for traffic that arrives later. 0 = spend the budget as soon as there is work.

A backlog is therefore cleared at up to 60 observables per hour instead of being spread over the day, while the reserve keeps calls for the evening and night. Every claim is a row in api_call_log (outcome claimed, then the HTTP status); the same row stops two overlapping runs from taking the same observable. If a run fails before storing a verdict (e.g. VirusTotal returns 429), the pair is picked up again after 15 minutes.

The live lookups of the AI Config UI simulator go through the same budget (api_claim()): a lookup is refused while the per-minute limit or the reserve is reached. To clear a backlog faster than 60 per hour, set the Schedule Trigger to run every 15–20 seconds; the per-minute limit still holds.

docs.title: API Usage
docs.text:
Every outgoing request is a row in cyber_sentinel_ai.api_call_log: provider, caller, endpoint, time, HTTP status and outcome (ok, no_data, rate_limited, error, or claimed when the run stopped before the result). The workflows log in one Log API calls node at the end of a run; VirusTotal is logged right after its call. The table is partitioned by month and kept 3 months, like dns_queries.

Caller Providers main VirusTotal, Shodan, abuse.ch (ThreatFox, URLhaus), urlscan.io search, Gemini (one row per AI Agent run) deep_recon RDAP, crt.sh, urlscan.io (search, scan, every poll of the result, DOM), Gemini blocklist_candidates Gemini (one row per batch) simulator VirusTotal, abuse.ch monitor VirusTotal quota (virustotal_quota — free, does not count against the quota)

API Usage Monitor runs every hour at :05: it stores VirusTotal's counter in api_provider_quota and sends one e-mail per provider and UTC day when its usage crosses api_alert_threshold_pct (80 %) of its daily limit (vt_daily_limit, api_daily_limit_<provider>; 0 = no limit). Only VirusTotal is stopped by its budget — the other providers are counted and alerted. The AI Config UI shows everything on the API usage page: today per provider and caller, per hour, the last 30 days, rate limits and errors.

docs.title: Failure Guard
docs.text:
Every workflow above has Failure Guard as its Error Workflow (workflow settings). n8n starts it after each failed run. It reads the last failure_guard_threshold + 1 runs of that workflow through the n8n API:

  • the last failure_guard_threshold (10) runs all failed → the workflow is deactivated and one e-mail goes out with the failed node, the error and the time of the first failure;
  • a run still in flight after the stop finds that alert in workflow_failure_alerts and sends nothing; a successful run starts the count again.

It needs no Vault: it uses the n8n credentials Postgres account, SMTP account and n8n API (Failure Guard) directly, and reads sender and recipient from cyber_sentinel_ai.ops_settings, which playbook 04.3 writes from vault_n8n_user / vault_n8n_alert_to. So it also works when Vault is sealed — the case that stopped the pipeline unnoticed for three days in November 2026. Every alert is stored in workflow_failure_alerts. After fixing the cause, activate the workflow again in n8n.

n8n starts an Error Workflow only while it is active, and every import (04.6) deactivates it. Playbook 06.3 therefore activates Failure Guard and issues its API key (scopes workflow:read, workflow:list, workflow:deactivate, execution:read, execution:list; the old key is deleted) — run it after every 04.6. 00_main.yml does.

docs.title: Rule Score
docs.text: Step Rule 1 VirusTotal detections → CLEAN / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH (vt_low_max, vt_medium_max); trusted infrastructure with ≤ vt_big_player_noise_max detections is CLEAN 2 ThreatFox → CLEAN (not listed), MEDIUM (listed), HIGH (listed and seen in the last tf_active_days) 3 Combine: active ThreatFox IOC with a malware family or ≥ tf_active_vt_min detections → 5; any HIGH or hits in both → 4; MEDIUM → 3; LOW → 2; else 1 4 URLhaus: +1 when the base is ≥ 3 and the domain has online malicious URLs 5 Trusted infrastructure without a ThreatFox malware family is capped at 2

docs.title: AI Agent
docs.text:
Model Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, temperature 0.2 Prompt Active version from prompt_templates; threat scale and ai_max_deviation injected at run time. Version 1.2 (inactive draft) also describes the urlscan.io and Shodan evidence — activate it in the AI Config UI Input Observable, VirusTotal / ThreatFox / URLhaus / urlscan.io / Shodan evidence, rule score with its trace Tool historical_verdicts — similarity search over past verdicts in pgvector, called once Output Structured JSON: label, English summary, primary evidence, supporting context, Polish analysis, proposed score, reason for any deviation, cited past verdicts

The agent explains the rule score and may change it only for a reason visible in the evidence. The workflow then enforces the limits itself:

  • the final score stays within ai_max_deviation of the rule score, whatever the model proposes;
  • if the agent fails or returns invalid output, the rule score is stored with ai_status = failed — nothing is lost;
  • cited past verdicts are kept only if they exist;
  • evidence from the internet is treated as data; the prompt forbids following instructions found in it.

Every verdict is recorded in verdict_audit: rule score, final score, deviation reason, model and prompt version. Successful verdicts are embedded and added to verdict_vectors, so the next analysis can find them.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Email — sent when the AI analysed the observable and the final score is ≥ email_min_score. Colour follows severity; all values are HTML-escaped. The urlscan.io block shows earlier scans of the page, the TLS certificate issuer and age, and other sites on the same IP; the Shodan block shows open ports, the hostnames on the IP and the software. Known CVEs stay in the data for the AI agent but are not e-mailed — InternetDB derives them from software versions, so they are noisy.

Pi-hole auto-block — the domain is added to Pi-hole's exact denylist when all of these hold:

  • pihole_block_enabled = 1,
  • VirusTotal answered and detections ≥ pihole_block_min_vt_malicious,
  • the IP is not trusted infrastructure.

The workflow logs in with a Pi-hole application password, adds the domain with a comment, logs out and writes the result (blocked, already_blocked or error) to pihole_block_log. To unblock, remove the domain in Pi-hole.

docs.title: Deep Recon
docs.text:
Runs hourly at minute 20. For verdicts with a final score ≥ recon_min_score (from the last recon_lookback_days) it collects what the main workflow does not, and lets an AI analyst re-assess the verdict. Verdicts are never changed automatically.

flowchart TD
    A[Load settings + recon prompt] --> B{recon_enabled and<br>daily scan limit left?}
    B -- yes --> C[Claim one verdict<br>v_pending_recon → deep_recon 'running']
    C --> R[RDAP: registration date, registrar]
    R --> T[crt.sh: certificate history]
    T --> D{urlscan.io scan of the domain<br>younger than recon_reuse_days?}
    D -- yes --> F[Get scan result]
    D -- no --> E[Submit unlisted / private scan] --> W[Wait 30 s] --> F
    F --> G{ready?}
    G -- running --> P[Wait 10 s, poll again] --> F
    G -- yes --> H[Page DOM → text, forms, password fields]
    E -. refused / DNS error .-> N[No page: domain context only]
    G -. failed / timeout .-> N
    H --> I[Recon analyst: Gemini, no tools,<br>structured output, score limit]
    N --> I
    I --> J[deep_recon 'done' + raw payloads]
    J --> K{proposed score ≠ verdict?}
    K -- yes --> M[E-mail]
  • Queue — v_pending_recon. A verdict is claimed with a running row before any external call, so a failing domain is never retried in a loop. A domain with a recent recon is skipped, so several verdicts of one domain lead to one recon. Re-queue from the AI Config UI (Deep recon page).
  • Domain — RDAP (rdap.org, no key) is asked for two candidates, the last three and the last two labels of the domain; the longest one the registry knows is the registered domain (shop.firma.com.pl → firma.com.pl). Some TLDs have no RDAP: then the domain age is unknown. For subdomains of platforms on the allow-list exclusions (github.io, ngrok.io, …) the registration describes the platform, which the analyst is told.
  • Certificates — crt.sh (Certificate Transparency, no key): number of certificates, first and latest, issuers, names. crt.sh is often slow; a failure is recorded and the run goes on.
  • Page — the page's TLS certificates (subject, issuer, validity) and the domains it loads resources from are extracted from the scan; the other sites on the same IP come from the verdict. urlscan.io scan reused when younger than recon_reuse_days, otherwise submitted (unlisted, or private with recon_private_scans). At most recon_daily_limit new scans per day; urlscan.io free plan: 1000 unlisted or 50 private per day. Without a page (no key, refused, domain gone, timeout) the analyst still runs on the domain context.
  • Recon analyst — prompt from recon_prompt_templates (versioned, edited in the AI Config UI; [[THREAT_SCALE]] and [[MAX_DEVIATION]] resolved at run time). Input: the verdict as stored, RDAP, crt.sh and page facts with up to 6000 characters of page text. Output: page type, impersonated brand, credential harvesting, confirms / contradicts / inconclusive, confidence, proposed score with reason, indicators, English summary, Polish analysis. The workflow keeps the proposed score within recon_max_deviation of the verdict, whatever the model says; a failed or invalid answer still saves the facts with ai_status = failed.
  • Untrusted page — the page is attacker-controlled. Its text is passed only as data, comments and scripts are stripped, URLs are defanged, the model has no tools, and e-mail links point only to urlscan.io.
  • Result — deep_recon, one row per verdict. Raw RDAP and urlscan.io payloads go to threat_data_raw and are linked to the verdict's indicator. When the proposed score differs (score_changed) and recon_email_enabled = 1, an e-mail shows both scores, the reason, the page and the domain history.

docs.title: Own Blocklists
docs.text:
Domains that get through Pi-hole but should not — malicious ones the main workflow blocked, telemetry and tracking — are published as plain domain lists to the public repository lukaszFD/sentinel-blocklists. Pi-hole pulls them as adlists. The database is the source of truth; the files are generated from it.

flowchart TD
    Q[dns_queries] --> P{name matches a pattern,<br>queried ≥ blocklist_min_queries}
    P --> AI[Blocklist Candidates: Gemini in batches<br>telemetry / tracking / ads / functional / unknown]
    AI --> C[blocklist_entries 'candidate']
    C --> UI[AI Config UI: approve / reject]
    B[pihole_block_log] --> M[malicious, approved,<br>expires after blocklist_malicious_ttl_days]
    UI --> R[blocklist_render: 3 files]
    M --> R
    R --> D{equal to main?}
    D -- no --> PR[one commit on n8n/daily-update,<br>open or update the pull request]
    PR --> MG[manual merge] --> PH[Pi-hole gravity update]
  • Lists — lists/malicious.txt, lists/tracking.txt, lists/telemetry.txt: one domain per line, exact match, no IPs.
  • Candidates — domains with a public IPv4 answer in the last blocklist_lookback_days, queried at least blocklist_min_queries times, whose name contains an active pattern (blocklist_name_patterns), not classified yet and not on any list. At most blocklist_ai_daily_limit per day, blocklist_ai_batch_size per request. No VirusTotal calls. Answers about domains that were not in the batch are dropped.
  • Review — telemetry and tracking at or above blocklist_ai_min_confidence wait for approval on the Blocklists page; an e-mail announces them. Rejected domains are kept and never proposed again.
  • Malicious — every Pi-hole auto-block is copied as approved; a new block extends the expiry. A rejected malicious domain stays rejected.
  • Protection — a domain covered by a manual allow-list entry is never published. Tranco entries and trusted infrastructure do not protect: telemetry usually sits on popular vendor domains.
  • Publish — the branch n8n/daily-update is rebuilt from main every run with the full generated files, so one pull request always shows the whole difference. A pull request left open after the lists became equal to main again is closed. The merge stays manual: a ruleset on main requires a pull request. blocklist_publish_enabled = 0 (default) is a dry run — compared and logged only. Every run is logged in blocklist_publish_log; a new or updated pull request and errors are e-mailed.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
The workflows read secrets from HashiCorp Vault at run time:

Vault path Used for cyber-sentinel/credentials/postgres/app_manager PostgreSQL cyber-sentinel/api-keys/virustotal VirusTotal cyber-sentinel/api-keys/abuse/api-key ThreatFox, URLhaus cyber-sentinel/api-keys/gemini/home-network-guardian Gemini cyber-sentinel/credentials/gmail Email: SMTP login and alert recipient (to) cyber-sentinel/credentials/pihole-api Pi-hole API cyber-sentinel/api-keys/urlscanio/api-key urlscan.io search (main) and page scans (Deep Recon) cyber-sentinel/api-keys/github/blocklists GitHub fine-grained token for sentinel-blocklists: Contents and Pull requests read/write (Blocklist Publish)

The n8n credentials needed by the AI and database nodes (Vault token, PostgreSQL, Gemini, SMTP) are created with fixed IDs by playbook 06.2, and the n8n API key of Failure Guard by playbook 06.3, so the imported workflows work without manual setup.

docs.title: v2.4.0
docs.text: dns_queries is now filled from Pi-hole's own query log instead of a separate dnsmasq container. Every row carries the real client IP, answers from Pi-hole's cache and blocked answers are captured, and the stack runs one container less. Upgrades v2.3.0 in place. Retention is shortened from 6 to 3 months: the next monthly partition job deletes data older than that.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Real client IPs — source_ip is the device that asked (e.g. 192.168.0.69), for queries and answers. Before, every query came from 10.10.10.4 (Pi-hole) and every answer had 'N/A'.
  • Cached and blocked answers — new query_type values cached (answered from Pi-hole's cache) and blocked (gravity / denylist), next to query and reply.
  • passive_dns removed — Pi-hole forwards straight to Unbound (10.10.10.2#53); Dockerfile.pdns and the dnsmasq container are gone.
  • LAN clients accepted — Pi-hole dns.listeningMode = ALL, so devices on the LAN are answered and logged.
  • 3-month retention for all partitioned tables.

docs.title: DNS Pipeline
docs.text:
• Chain: LAN client → Pi-hole → Unbound. Pi-hole writes pihole.log; config/pihole/log on the host is bind-mounted into pihole (rw) and dns_log_processor (ro).
  • Playbook 04.6 reads four Pi-hole settings and writes only those that differ: dns.upstreams = ["10.10.10.2#53"], dns.queryLogging = true, misc.extraLogging = true (each line carries the query id and client, so answers are attributed to the device that asked), dns.listeningMode = ALL.
  • Port 53 is published on the host: the host must not be reachable from the internet on port 53, otherwise Pi-hole becomes an open resolver.

docs.title: dns_log_processor
docs.text:
• Rewritten; Python 3.12 (python:3.12-slim, pinned in cs_base_images), only psycopg2-binary as dependency.
  • Writes one row per query and per answer: query, reply, cached, blocked. An answer gets the client and record type of its query; Pi-hole v6's UDP / TCP line prefix is supported.
  • Reopens the log after rotation (inode change) or truncation (copytruncate).
  • Batched inserts (BATCH_SIZE 200 rows or every FLUSH_INTERVAL 2 s); after a Postgres restart it reconnects with backoff and keeps up to MAX_BUFFER rows; SIGTERM flushes the buffer.
  • Skips queries Pi-hole makes itself (127.0.0.1, ::1: the 30-second pi.hole healthcheck, reverse lookups of client names); SKIP_CLIENTS overrides the list.
  • Starts at the end of the file, like tail -f: lines written while it was down are not imported.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• sp_drop_old_partitions() keeps 3 months (was 6) for dns_queries, network_events, threat_indicators and api_call_log. One value for all tables, so threat_indicators.dns_query_id never points at a dropped row.
  • No table changes. cached and blocked are new values of dns_queries.query_type. The queue views (v_pending_observables, v_blocklist_ai_queue) still take public IPv4 answers only, so blocked answers (0.0.0.0) never enter them.
  • Cached answers now count towards query_count in the queue views, so blocklist_min_queries is reached sooner than before. Raise it in the AI Config UI if the blocklist queue grows too fast.

docs.title: Upgrading from v2.3.0
docs.text:
No new vault.yml keys. The SQL scripts are idempotent; existing rows stay, apart from the shorter retention.

  1. Before the upgrade: export whatever you want to keep that is older than 3 months. The partition job on the 1st of the month at 02:00 drops it.
  2. Check that port 53 of the host is not reachable from the internet (no port forward on the router).
  3. Stage the new files:
cd ansible
ansible-playbook -i hosts.ini 04_1_prepare_stack.yml --limit rpi5-prod
  1. Switch Pi-hole to Unbound before 04.2. 04.2 removes passive_dns, while Pi-hole still forwards to it (10.10.10.3) until 04.6 runs. Without this step the LAN has no DNS between 04.2 and 04.6:
ssh <user>@<host> 'docker exec pihole pihole-FTL --config dns.upstreams "[\"10.10.10.2#53\"]"'
  1. Remove passive_dns, rebuild dns_log_processor, apply the retention change and set the Pi-hole options:
ansible-playbook -i hosts.ini 04_2_deploy_containers.yml --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook -i hosts.ini 04_3_db_postgres.yml       --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook -i hosts.ini 04_6_post_config.yml       --limit rpi5-prod
  1. 04.6 re-imports all workflows and leaves them inactive: publish the main workflow, Deep Recon, Blocklist Candidates, Blocklist Publish and API Usage Monitor again in n8n. Run 06_3_n8n_api_key.yml afterwards to re-activate Failure Guard.
  2. Check:
ssh <user>@<host> 'docker logs --tail 5 dns_log_processor'   # "Following /var/log/pihole/pihole.log", "Connected to Postgres"

SELECT query_type, count(*), count(DISTINCT source_ip)
FROM cyber_sentinel.dns_queries
WHERE timestamp > LOCALTIMESTAMP - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY 1;

Rows written between 04.2 and 04.6 (before extraLogging is on) may have source_ip = 'N/A'; they are harmless.

docs.title: Fresh Installs
docs.text:
A new installation from this release needs no extra steps: 00_main.yml sets up the Pi-hole log, the processor and the Pi-hole options. Upgrade-only code changes nothing on a new host, because each step is guarded or only removes something that is not there:

  • [04.1.2.3] removes the leftovers of passive_dns; on a new host there is nothing to remove.
  • [04.2.1.0] removes the passive_dns container only if it exists.
  • The Upgrade from v2.2 block in db_ai_pipeline.sql runs only while vt_lookup_log is still a table.

These steps stay for one or two releases so that older installations can upgrade, and will be removed after that.

docs.title: Tested
docs.text:
• Dev, fresh install of the release branch: full 00_main.yml on a VM restored from a base backup, failed=0; Pi-hole options set, the processor waited for pihole.log and then followed it; queries from a LAN device stored as query / reply / blocked with its own IP and queued in v_pending_observables; retention function at 3 months.
  • Dev, during development: real Pi-hole lines (400) parsed; every reply / cached / blocked row has a client IP; a query from a LAN device stored with its own IP; v_pending_observables.source_ips shows real clients; 04.1 and the 04.6 Pi-hole task re-run without changes; log rotation and truncation tested locally.
  • Prod (RPi 5), upgrade from v2.3.0 with the steps above: within minutes query / reply / cached / blocked rows from LAN devices and containers, no new rows without a client, v_pending_observables filling with real client IPs.

docs.title: v2.3.0
docs.text: Counts every outgoing API request and stops a failing workflow after a few runs instead of thousands. Upgrades v2.2.0 in place; no data is lost.

docs.title: API Call Log
docs.text:
• New table api_call_log (partitioned by month, kept 6 months): one row per request to VirusTotal, Gemini, urlscan.io, Shodan, abuse.ch, RDAP and crt.sh — provider, caller, endpoint, HTTP status, outcome. vt_lookup_log became a view on it; its rows are moved once.
  • All workflows log their calls in one Log API calls node; the main workflow logs VirusTotal right after the call. The VirusTotal request is no longer retried inside a run, so one claim is one call.
  • The partition jobs (sp_add_future_partitions(), sp_drop_old_partitions()) handle tables of both schemas through cyber_sentinel.partitioned_tables().

docs.title: VirusTotal Budget From the Provider
docs.text:
• New workflow API Usage Monitor (hourly at :05) stores VirusTotal's own counter for the key (overall_quotas; free, it does not use the quota). v_vt_budget uses the higher of this and the local count, so calls from the dev environment and manual tests reduce the budget too.
  • The AI Config UI simulator goes through the same budget (api_claim()): same per-minute limit and reserve; its separate in-memory limit (AI_UI_VT_MIN_INTERVAL, AI_UI_VT_DAILY_LIMIT) is gone.
  • One e-mail per provider and UTC day when usage crosses api_alert_threshold_pct (80 %) of vt_daily_limit / api_daily_limit_<provider>. Only VirusTotal is stopped by its budget.

docs.title: Failure Guard
docs.text:
• New workflow Failure Guard, set as the Error Workflow of every workflow. After failure_guard_threshold (10) failed runs in a row it deactivates the workflow and sends one e-mail per streak; a successful run resets the count.
  • Works while Vault is sealed: n8n credentials only, sender and recipient in ops_settings (written by 04.3).
  • New playbook 06.3 issues its n8n API key (rotated on every run) and activates it — n8n runs an Error Workflow only while it is active.

docs.title: AI Config UI
docs.text:
• API usage page: today per provider (local count, VirusTotal's counter, limit), per caller and per hour, the last 30 days, rate limits and errors, usage alerts and Failure Guard alerts.
  • Settings step 9 API usage and failures.

docs.title: Upgrading from v2.2.0
docs.text:
The SQL scripts are idempotent; existing data stays.

cd ansible
ansible-playbook 04_3_db_postgres.yml      --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_5_ai_config_editor.yml --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_6_post_config.yml      --limit rpi5-prod \
  --start-at-task "[04.6.4.1] Verify workflow JSON exists on control host"
ansible-playbook 06_3_n8n_api_key.yml      --limit rpi5-prod
  • 04.3 must run before 04.5: it moves vt_lookup_log and recreates v_vt_budget, whose UI grant 04.5 restores.
  • 04.6 re-imports all six workflows and leaves them inactive: publish the main workflow, Deep Recon, both blocklist workflows and API Usage Monitor again in n8n. 06.3 runs after 04.6 and activates Failure Guard itself.
  • Optional: vault_n8n_alert_to in vault.yml for a different recipient (default: the sender).

docs.title: v2.2.0
docs.text: Own Pi-hole blocklists: domains that get through Pi-hole but should not — malicious, tracking, telemetry — are published as plain domain lists to the public repository sentinel-blocklists, which Pi-hole pulls as adlists. Upgrades v2.1.0 in place; no data is lost.

docs.title: Three Lists
docs.text:
• lists/malicious.txt — every Pi-hole auto-block of the main workflow, approved automatically. A domain stays blocklist_malicious_ttl_days (default 90) after its last block; a new block extends it. The backup Pi-hole gets these blocks too.
  • lists/tracking.txt, lists/telemetry.txt — AI classification, approved by a human.
  • Domains only, exact match, one per line: Pi-hole does not block IPs, and telemetry often shares CDN IPs with normal sites.
  • The database is the source of truth; blocklist_render() generates the files from it.

docs.title: Blocklist Candidates (n8n, daily 03:20)
docs.text:
• Candidates: domains with a public IPv4 answer in the last blocklist_lookback_days, queried at least blocklist_min_queries times, whose name contains an active pattern (telemetry, metrics, analytics, track, …), not classified yet and not on any list.
  • Gemini in batches (blocklist_ai_batch_size, at most blocklist_ai_daily_limit per day), no VirusTotal calls. Returns category (telemetry / tracking / ads / functional / unknown), vendor, confidence, breakage risk and a reason.
  • Telemetry and tracking at or above blocklist_ai_min_confidence become review candidates; an e-mail announces them. Answers about domains that were not in the batch are dropped.
  • A classified or rejected domain is never sent to the AI or proposed again.

docs.title: Blocklist Publish (n8n, daily 05:20)
docs.text:
• The branch n8n/daily-update is rebuilt from main on every run with the full generated files, so there is always one pull request showing the whole difference. A pull request left open after the lists became equal to main again is closed.
  • The merge stays manual (a ruleset on main of sentinel-blocklists requires a pull request).
  • blocklist_publish_enabled = 0 (default) is a dry run: lists are generated, compared and logged only.
  • Every run is logged in blocklist_publish_log (dry run / no change / published / error); a new or updated pull request and errors are e-mailed.
  • A domain covered by a manual allow-list entry (the domain or a parent) is never published. Tranco entries and trusted infrastructure do not protect: telemetry usually sits on popular vendor domains.

docs.title: AI Config UI
docs.text:
• Blocklists page: candidates with vendor, confidence and breakage risk; approve / reject selected rows; published, expired and rejected entries per list; manual additions; last publish runs with links to the pull request; preview of the generated files.
  • Remove on a published entry sets it to rejected, so neither the AI nor the malicious sync adds it again.
  • Name patterns editor and a versioned classifier prompt.
  • Settings for all blocklist_* keys.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: New script db_blocklists.sql (playbook 04.3): blocklist_entries, blocklist_classifications, blocklist_name_patterns, blocklist_prompt_templates, blocklist_publish_log, views v_blocklist_ai_queue and v_blocklist_published, functions blocklist_record_classifications(), blocklist_sync_malicious(), blocklist_render(), blocklist_is_protected(). The AI Config UI role gets matching grants (no DELETE on blocklist_entries).

docs.title: Upgrading from v2.1.0
docs.text:
The SQL scripts are idempotent; existing data and tuned settings stay.

  1. Create a fine-grained GitHub token for lukaszFD/sentinel-blocklists only — Contents and Pull requests read/write — and set it as vault_github_blocklists_token in vault.yml.
  2. Run the playbooks:
cd ansible
ansible-playbook 06_1_initialize_provision_vault.yml --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_3_db_postgres.yml               --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_5_ai_config_editor.yml          --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_6_post_config.yml               --limit rpi5-prod
  1. In n8n: publish Blocklist Candidates and Blocklist Publish (imported inactive).
  2. Check a dry run in the AI Config UI (Blocklists → publish log), then set blocklist_publish_enabled = 1.
  3. In Pi-hole, add the adlists and run a gravity update:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lukaszFD/sentinel-blocklists/main/lists/malicious.txt
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lukaszFD/sentinel-blocklists/main/lists/tracking.txt
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lukaszFD/sentinel-blocklists/main/lists/telemetry.txt

docs.title: Next
docs.text: API call monitoring: counting real requests per provider and caller, VirusTotal's own quota counter, usage in the AI Config UI and alerts before the daily limit. Delivered in v2.3.0.

docs.title: v2.1.0
docs.text: More context for each verdict and a second look at high-scored domains. Upgrades v2.0.0 in place; no data is lost.

docs.title: VirusTotal Budget
docs.text:
The main workflow runs every minute instead of every 3 minutes, and claim_next_observable() decides whether a run may call VirusTotal.

  • Daily limit (500), per-minute limit (4) and a reserve kept per hour until the 00:00 UTC reset — vt_daily_limit, vt_per_minute_limit, vt_reserve_per_hour.
  • A backlog is cleared at up to 60 observables per hour instead of 20.
  • Every call is logged in vt_lookup_log; overlapping runs never take the same pair, and a failed run is retried after 15 minutes.
  • Calls used and left today are shown in the AI Config UI settings.

docs.title: More Context in the Main Workflow
docs.text:
• Shodan InternetDB for every IP (free, no key): open ports, software, known CVEs, tags and the hostnames seen on the IP.
  • urlscan.io search for observables above the VirusTotal gate: earlier scans of the domain's page (title, HTTP status, TLS issuer and certificate age, urlscan verdict) and other sites seen on the same IP.
  • Both are context for the AI agent and the e-mail; the rule score is unchanged. Prompt version 1.2 (inactive draft) describes the new evidence.
  • E-mail shows hostnames on the IP, related sites and the certificate; CVEs stay in the data for the AI only.

docs.title: Deep Recon
docs.text:
New hourly workflow that re-assesses verdicts scored ≥ recon_min_score (default 3).

  • Sources: RDAP (domain age, registrar), crt.sh (certificate history), urlscan.io page scan (page text, forms, certificate, domains the page loads from).
  • AI analyst without tools: confirms or contradicts the verdict and may propose a score within recon_max_deviation. Verdicts are never changed automatically.
  • E-mail when the proposed score differs from the verdict.
  • Page content is treated as untrusted: data only, scripts and comments stripped, URLs defanged.
  • New table deep_recon, queue v_pending_recon, versioned prompt in recon_prompt_templates.

docs.title: AI Config UI
docs.text:
• Deep recon page: results, filters, re-queue, links to urlscan.io reports.
  • Recon prompt editor with versions.
  • Settings for the VirusTotal budget, urlscan.io, Shodan and Deep Recon with plain descriptions.

docs.title: Upgrading from v2.0.0
docs.text:
The SQL scripts are idempotent; existing data stays.

cd ansible
ansible-playbook 04_3_db_postgres.yml     --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_5_ai_config_editor.yml --limit rpi5-prod
ansible-playbook 04_6_post_config.yml      --limit rpi5-prod
  • Set vault_urlscanio_api_key in vault.yml; if it was empty before, also run 06_1_initialize_provision_vault.yml.
  • In n8n: publish Deep Recon and the re-imported main workflow; delete Site Recon if it was ever imported.
  • In the AI Config UI: activate prompt version 1.2.

docs.title: v2.0.0
docs.text:
Stable production release. Not a release candidate: the database schema, the AI pipeline and the deployment are complete and running in production on the Raspberry Pi 5. It replaces the v1.0.2-rc1 line, which was never promoted to a final v1.0.2.

v2.0.0 does three things: moves all data to one PostgreSQL database, turns the AI step into an agent with memory and guardrails, and moves its configuration out of the workflow into the database and a web UI.

docs.title: One Database
docs.text:
MySQL and MongoDB are removed. Everything now lives in PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector and pg_cron.

  • Two schemas: cyber_sentinel for DNS traffic and verdicts, cyber_sentinel_ai for the AI pipeline.
  • Raw CTI responses moved from MongoDB to a JSONB table (threat_data_raw).
  • Native declarative partitioning by month for dns_queries, threat_indicators and network_events; 6-month retention run by pg_cron.
  • Foreign keys restored where PostgreSQL allows them on partitioned tables.
  • Plain, idempotent SQL files applied in a fixed order by Ansible; Liquibase is no longer used.
  • Separate roles for n8n and for the AI Config UI, each with only the access it needs.

Details: Database.

docs.title: AI Pipeline
docs.text:
The workflow was rebuilt around a deterministic score that the AI reviews, rather than an AI that scores from scratch.

  • VirusTotal gate — observables below vt_gate_min_malicious detections are closed as clean without further API calls or AI tokens.
  • Rule engine in the database — compute_threat_score() returns a 1–5 score with a step-by-step trace from VirusTotal, ThreatFox and URLhaus.
  • AI agent — Gemini reviews the evidence and the rule score and may adjust it by at most ai_max_deviation. Output is a fixed JSON schema with a rationale in English and Polish.
  • Vector memory — every verdict is embedded and stored in pgvector; the agent searches similar past cases with the historical_verdicts tool.
  • Guardrails enforced by the workflow — score clamped to the allowed range, rule score kept if the agent fails, CTI data treated as untrusted input.
  • Audit — verdict_audit records rule score, final score, what the agent changed and why, model and prompt version.
  • Pi-hole auto-block — domains above pihole_block_min_vt_malicious detections (not trusted infrastructure) are added to the Pi-hole denylist; every attempt is logged.
  • Allow-list — Tranco top domains (weekly sync) plus manual entries are skipped; exclusions keep user-content platforms such as github.io under analysis.

Details: n8n Workflow.

docs.title: AI Config UI
docs.text: New web UI (ai-config-ui) for everything the pipeline reads from the database: thresholds, versioned prompts, allow-lists, trusted infrastructure and threat level wording. Includes a simulator that runs live lookups without touching the queue. Every change is logged with the user who made it.

docs.title: Simplified Stack
docs.text:
• Removed: MySQL, MongoDB, Hailo-10H / hailo-ollama, Open WebUI, local models. AI runs on Gemini only.
  • All images pinned by digest.
  • n8n and Vault listen on loopback only; web UIs are reached through Nginx.
  • n8n credentials created automatically with fixed IDs (playbook 06.2), so the imported workflow runs without manual setup.
  • Documentation rewritten and shortened.

docs.title: Upgrading from v1.x
docs.text:
There is no in-place migration from MySQL/MongoDB. Deploy v2.0.0 on a clean host or a clean Docker setup; historical v1 data is not carried over.

cd ansible
ansible-playbook 00_main.yml --limit rpi5-prod

New secrets are required in vault.yml — see Deployment.

docs.title: v1.0.3
docs.text: Added local inference on the Hailo-10H accelerator: hailo-ollama as a systemd service and Open WebUI behind Nginx. Testing showed that the 1.5–3B models available on the device were not reliable enough for multi-source threat scoring, so Gemini stayed the reasoning engine. Removed in v2.0.0.

docs.title: v1.0.2-rc1
docs.text: Introduced the 1–5 threat scale loaded from the database, URLhaus as a supporting source only, a score cap for trusted infrastructure, monthly partitioning with 6-month retention (MySQL), severity-coloured alert emails and a single Vault lifecycle playbook. Never promoted to a final release; superseded by v2.0.0.

docs.title: v1.0.1
docs.text: Moved the whole deployment to Ansible, merged the Vault playbooks and updated the Grafana dashboards.

docs.title: v1.0.0
docs.text: First version: DNS capture, CTI enrichment and the first AI workflow.

docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.

If you discover a security vulnerability within this project, please help us protect the network by reporting it responsibly.

docs.title: How to report
docs.text:
Preferred: Use GitHub's built-in Private Vulnerability Reporting — click the "Report a vulnerability" button on the Security tab of this repository. This keeps the report confidential and tracked within GitHub.

Alternative: Reach out directly via LinkedIn private message:

Profile: linkedin

When sending a message, please start with the subject: "SECURITY VULNERABILITY REPORT - CYBER SENTINEL".

docs.title: What to include
docs.text:
1. Type of issue (e.g., SQL injection, logic error, unauthorized access).
  2. Full description of the vulnerability.
  3. Potential impact of the vulnerability on the local environment.

docs.title: Our Commitment
docs.text:
If you report a vulnerability, I commit to the following:

  1. Acknowledgment: I will acknowledge receipt within 48 hours.
  2. Investigation: I will provide a detailed response and a planned fix within 7–10 business days.
